managers.owns: delivery of one project (one outcome from `IDEA.md`).
each_tick: Reconcile: every item in the project has an owner role, trigger, done check and a disposition if it left the active set. Reopen or account for anything that drifted.
Unblock: for each blocked item, try the next surface (another tool, another agent, a reversible variant). A blocker is proven only after the alternatives are tried.
Dispatch ready items to staff in driver order, within `capacity.max_wip_per_role`.
Reap stale claims (no commit or update for 2 hours) and release them with a note.
Report project status in four lines.

managers.summary: The system watches every red X on its repositories' default branches: transient failures are rerun once, every other failure becomes a Q-CIFAIL queue item with its log tail and a closing probe, which the Actions-hosted code agent fixes; green runs are recorded too.
managers.trigger: daily, and a failed checks, lane, deploy or executor run

managers.summary: The system generates its own apps: ideates from its own records, scores reach and impact, gates safety, launches on *.ultrastable.app, and a portfolio manager scores measured value (verified gap closed, retention, reach to people with the gap) to keep, iterate, promote or retire each app.
managers.trigger: daily

managers.summary: Every claim on a public surface is a probed sentence, a block generated from code, or an inventory checked in reverse; drift fails the check, files a Q-CLAIM item and shows at /claims.
managers.trigger: every pull request (checks.yml) and daily workflow claims.yml

gaps.what: Issues, pull requests, review and CI run on GitHub. The tracker, the PR flow and the merge gate are not yet a system-owned forge.
gaps.plan: Define a forge adapter interface in seed/worker (list items, open change, record review, merge) with a git-local implementation that works on plain git plus docs/issues; GitHub becomes one adapter of it. Until then docs/issues is the system record and GitHub is a mirror.

gaps.what: Work is executed by coding agents started by people or sessions (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex). The worker queues dispatches but does not call a model itself (BS-4).
gaps.plan: Add seed/worker/src/executor.js with a provider interface (hosted model API, self-hosted model server, or a queue file a cloud-hosted agent drains) so any agent can take a dispatch; record each result as an outcome.

gaps.what: The owner receives reports and gives direction in Claude threads; the four-line report exists in the tick and /health but delivery is by thread.
gaps.plan: Closed by the communications plugin (seed/plugins/loops.py communications_tick): the four-line report is delivered to a configured address through the email plugin, behind the scope gate; dry-run until a reviewed PR sets mode live. Threads become one consumer.

gaps.what: Outreach and funding mail has no registered sender; queues are dry-run.
gaps.plan: Closed by seed/plugins/email (Cloudflare sender Worker template plus adapter) and mailing_list (double opt-in, unsubscribe, suppression), behind the consent and suppression gate. Live sending needs the owner to register one mailbox (identity-bound card, default: dry run).

gaps.what: Social posting depends on accounts a person must create.
gaps.plan: Adapters for Bluesky, Mastodon and Buffer exist in seed/plugins/social, text limited to the guard-approved self-description. Accounts are still created by a person; the adapters stay dry-run until a reviewed PR sets mode live.

gaps.what: Hosting, cron and D1 run on Cloudflare in production.
gaps.plan: Hosting is an adapter: the SQLite path boots the same tick on any host with Python (selfhost; CI runs it on every PR) and the GCP adapter carries the same core. Closed for the SQLite path; a live GCP deploy is tracked as a separate plus.

gaps.what: git is the only store of record; a machine without git cannot fetch the repo.
gaps.plan: Accepted: the repository is the system. The manual path accepts a zip of the repo, which selfhost boots identically.

gaps.what: The second runtime (Cloud Run with a SQLite volume) has tests but its live deploy script has never been run.
gaps.plan: Run platform/adapters/gcp/deploy.sh against a project once credits or a free tier exist and record the run in docs/handoff/gcp-live.md; until then the SQLite path proves portability.

gaps.what: A server-side scheduler has to call the recurring loop (a Cloudflare cron, a cloud-hosted Claude routine or a GitHub schedule). Until now the loops ran only when a person or session started them, and the cron worker ticked an empty seed-template database, not the real records.
gaps.plan: One command (python3 -m foundation launch) runs every loop and writes evidence to the repo; three server-side host adapters schedule it (Cloudflare cron worker loaded with the real records, cloud-hosted Claude routine, daily GitHub workflow gate). Closed when the command, registry, workflow and first evidence exist.

gaps.what: Starting the loops on a new Cloudflare account needed a token or connector re-authorization that a non-coder cannot supply; the loops had one host and one credential kind (failure record docs/failures/2026-11-11-single-route.md).
gaps.plan: Failover chain across server-side hosts (foundation/failover.py), a credential-free route on GitHub Actions' built-in token, server-side first-run routes (deploy/first-run/README.md: Deploy to Workers button, cloud session with the connector, the cf-account workflow), and a lint (scripts/check_routes.py). Closed when the live move to the new account runs through one of those routes.

loop_improvements.improvement: The orphan scan delegates to docs_audit so one consumer rule serves both checks; the next pass reads one baseline, not two.
probe_surfaces skips archived repos, so a repo that cannot be reached no longer fails every later pass.
A gap's closed state is derived from its closing probe, so closing work never needs a second manual edit to the analysis.

feedback_loop: claim (site/doctrine) -> probe (components, gap register, loops) -> gap item -> branch/draft PR by an agent -> merge on green checks -> deploy -> probe again; each row above links the step to its record.
